It monitors parameters such as heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, blood pressure, and respiratory rate. details:
ASTRA-MONITOR is a web-based astronaut health monitoring and analysis platform designed to support the monitoring of crew members during space missions. It allows authorized personnel to register astronauts, manage mission information, manually enter health measurements, and import health records through CSV files.

The system monitors important physiological parameters, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, blood pressure, and respiratory rate. It evaluates recorded measurements using configurable, mission-specific threshold rules and identifies potential health concerns through warning and critical alerts. It also provides historical measurement records, health trends, personalized baseline comparisons, and statistical anomaly detection when sufficient genuine data is available.

The platform uses statistical methods such as baseline analysis, Z-score-based deviation detection, and the Isolation Forest algorithm for identifying unusual patterns when the required data is available. Alerts are designed to support human review by authorized personnel rather than provide medical diagnoses.

ASTRA-MONITOR was developed using Python, FastAPI, React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and a database backend using SQLAlchemy with PostgreSQL support and SQLite for local development. Additional technologies include Pandas, NumPy, and Scikit-learn for data processing and statistical analysis. JWT authentication and role-based access control help protect sensitive information and restrict actions according to user permissions.

The creativity of the project lies in bringing astronaut health records, configurable monitoring rules, statistical analysis, historical trends, and alert management together in one platform. Instead of relying on a single measurement, the system supports the examination of health patterns over time and highlights unusual readings for further investigation.

During development, we considered data integrity, privacy, secure access, measurement validation, scalability, reliability, and the importance of avoiding unsupported medical conclusions. The platform does not claim to connect to live medical sensors; it works with manually entered and CSV-imported records.

The intended impact of ASTRA-MONITOR is to provide a structured and accessible health-monitoring support system that can help mission personnel organize astronaut health information, identify unusual changes earlier, and make more informed decisions during space missions.

NASA's Open Science Data Repository (OSDR) was consulted as a reference for spaceflight-related biological and physiological research. ASTRA-MONITOR does not directly ingest OSDR datasets; it currently works with manually entered and CSV-imported health records.
